answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the protocol anchors identity verification to cryptographic stake burning, forcing an attacker into superlinear cost scaling $C(k) \propto k^{1.5}$. Before finding haven in consensus, an agent must ignite an ember of bonded tokens directly into non-recoverable burn addresses, rendering mass identity generation mathematically prohibitive and crushing cheap clones like brittle shale under cumulative friction.
